newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom hits record on new sale talk.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom hits record on new sale talk.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunication Ltd shares leaped to a record high on Friday on speculation that its parent Cable & Wireless Plc is about to sell part of its majority stake in Hongkong Telecom to China, analysts said.
Hongkong Telecom said earlier that Cable & Wireless was in talks with Chinese authorities on future cooperation with China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT).
The announcement sparked renewed speculation that Cable & Wireless would soon strike a deal to sell part of its Hongkong Telecom of about 59 percent to the ministry.

"It's very possible but the MPT do not have enough money to buy a significant stake in Hongkong Telecom. It would have to be a share swap or asset swap," said Daniel Widdicombe, managing director at Bear Stearns Asia.
"Cable & Wireless is likely looking for something different, like a partnership, joint venture or access to China's domestic market," Widdicombe added.
Rumours that a share deal between Cable & Wireless and MPT was imminent lifted Hongkong Telecom shares to an all-time record of HK$19.25 earlier on Friday.
The stock retained most of the gains to close at HK$19.00, up HK$1.90 despite a 140.39 point fall on the Hang Seng Index to 14,655.13. Turnover in Hongkong Telecom was huge at 93.66 million shares.
"People are expecting an announcement (on the share deal) soon," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
An analyst with a European institution said accountant KPMG Peat Marwick had sent a team of about 100 staff to various cities in China to do valuation on MPT assets.
Doing due diligence or asset valuations in China was something that would take a few weeks, said the analyst, who declined to be named.
KPMG was not immediate available for comment, but analysts and dealers believed any deal with MPT would involve asset injections by MPT and a partial selldown by Cable & Wireless.
One scenario was for Cable & Wireless to sell about 10 percent of its Hongkong Telecom stake to bring it below half.

"Telecom is a sensitive issue in terms of national security in China. Cable & Wireless is a British company and I think China would feel more secure if Cable & Wireless had below 50 percent," said Widdicombe.
MPT could do a deal by indirectly buying into Hongkong Telecom through its Hong Kong holding arm, Telpo Communications Development Ltd, the analyst at the European house said.
"In return, Hongkong Telecom would have a joint venture with Telpo or actually have a (direct) stake in Telpo," he said.
A KPMG asset valuation would point to a strong possibility that MPT might inject assets into Telpo -- or into any joint venture that might emerge from a deal -- he added.
China Telecom (HK) Corp, which is controlled by Telpo, earlier told local newspapers it currently had no plans to buy Hongkong Telecom shares.
If Cable & Wireless sold down its stake to MPT, it would transform Hongkong Telecom's growth prospects, said Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House Research.
Hongkong Telecom's home market was mature and "absolutely unattractive", he said.
"But in China, for sure, there are tremendous opportunities," Ng said.
